    Finite integral halfspace tests for a rational cone #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.Farkas.finite_feasibility_tests (n : ℕ) {I : Type u_1} [Fintype I] (A : I → Fin n → ℚ) :
    ∃ (S : Finset (I → ℚ)), ∀ (b : I → ℚ), Feasible A b ↔ ∀ s ∈ S, ∑ i : I, s i * b i ≤ 0

    With the coefficient matrix fixed, elimination gives a single finite list of tests that decides feasibility for every right-hand side.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.Farkas.finite_cone_tests {n m : ℕ} (V : Fin m → Fin n → ℤ) :
    ∃ (H : Finset (Fin n → ℤ)), ∀ (z : Fin n → ℤ), (∀ h ∈ H, 0 ≤ ∑ t : Fin n, h t * z t) ↔ ∃ (a : Fin m → ℚ), (∀ (i : Fin m), 0 ≤ a i) ∧ ∀ (t : Fin n), ↑(z t) = ∑ i : Fin m, a i * ↑(V i t)

    A finite system of rational linear inequalities recognizes the nonnegative rational span of a finite list of integral vectors.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.Farkas.finite_lattice_cone_tests {G : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup G] {n m : ℕ} (v : Fin n → G →+ ℤ) (hv : Function.Injective fun (z : G) (t : Fin n) => (v t) z) (X : Fin m → G) :
    ∃ (H : Finset (Fin n → ℤ)), ∀ (z : G), (∀ h ∈ H, 0 ≤ (∑ t : Fin n, h t • v t) z) ↔ ∃ (p : ℤ) (a : Fin m → ℤ), 0 < p ∧ (∀ (i : Fin m), 0 ≤ a i) ∧ p • z = ∑ i : Fin m, a i • X i

    On an integral lattice the same tests detect a relation after clearing one positive denominator on the class being tested.
